newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Cimentas aims to raise 1997 sales by 25 pct.
newsitem.headline: Turk Cimentas aims to raise 1997 sales by 25 pct.

text.p: Turkish cement and breeze block producer Cimentas Izmir Cimento Fabrikasi Turk A.S. aims to increase net sales by 25 percent to $100 million in 1997 from $80 million in 1996, a senior company official said on Friday.

"Good weather conditions pushed up our sales and prices in the first quarter and it will make it easier for us to meet the $100 million turnover target," general manager Ahmet Vasfi Pekin told Reuters.
Total cement sales of the company rose by 27.2 percent to 173,000 tonnes in the first two months of this year.
Shares of the company opened at 19,000 lira on Friday on the Istanbul Stock Exchange and closed at 19,250 lira.

The company is planning to sell 1.8 million tonnes of cement -- worth $74 million -- in 1997. About 1.3 million tonnes of the output, worth $58 million, will be sold in the domestic market and the rest abroad.
The company is expected to generate about $26 million of turnover from the sale of 540,000 cubic metres of breeze blocks and 210,000 square metres of floor and wall tiles.

Cimentas began to produce floor and wall tiles this year after a $12 million investment in 1996. It also expanded its breeze block production capacity to 745,000 cubic metres in 1996 from 295,000 cubic metres after a 45 million German mark investment was completed at its plant in the central Anatolian town of Kirkkale.
The company is the sole breeze block producer in the Aegean and central Anatolian regions.
It bought a small-scale state-owned cement factory, Kars Cimento, from the privatisation administration for $22.5 million in 1996.
"Assets of the company soared with the effect of the massive investment programme," Pekin said. "For this reason increased depreciation lowered our net profit."
Financial expenses of the company soared to 803.5 billion lira in 1996 from 7.1 billion in 1995 and its net profit shrank to 591 billion lira from 947 billion.
It reported 7.1 trillion lira of total sales in 1996, against 3.6 trillion in 1995.
Pekin said Cimentas would set up a new cement plant in the Aegean region when "a suitable place" is found and the financial effects of the recent investments are eliminated.
